content.value: Implement accessors, mutators, and helpers; use parameters and return values correctly; cover every normal return path.

A method body implements the contract stated by its header and documentation. An accessor typically returns information without changing the object, while a mutator updates state. A helper performs a smaller operation used by another method. Choose a return type that matches the promised result, or void for an action with no result.

return ends the current invocation and sends a value back when required. All reachable normal completion paths in a non-void method must provide a compatible value. Printing and returning are separate actions. Primitive parameter values are copied from arguments, so assigning a parameter does not reassign the caller’s variable.

For larger(7, 4), the condition is true and the method immediately returns 7. For larger(4, 7), execution reaches the second return and also yields 7. Equal arguments take the first branch and return their common value. No input is changed.

A println statement does not satisfy a return requirement. Forgetting the fallback return can make a method fail compilation. Avoid returning before a necessary update, and avoid unreachable statements after an unconditional return.
Implement isEven(int value) to return whether value % 2 == 0. It can be a single return statement. Then test positive, negative, and zero inputs; zero is even.
